To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the optimization of PET reconstruction parameters can be used to improve the quantitative accuracy of PET images in multicentre trials.

(i) the optimization of the reconstruction parameters of 3D-Osem PET images for multicentre trials should be based on a phantom study; (ii) the optimized reconstruction parameters can be applied to the clinical data without any additional effort; (iii) the optimized reconstruction improves the quantitative results of multicenter PET studies.
(1) the use of Jaszczak and Hoffman phantoms in PET centres allows to optimize PET quantitative values to a high level per site, while decreasing variability across centres.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new imaging techniques and the improvement of image quality.
optimizing the acquisition and reconstruction parameters of PET scanners for multicentre trials in order to reduce variability across centres.
the optimization of quantitative PET imaging in a multicentre trial, in the context of a French initiative launched to handle the neuroimage of a large cohort.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the optimized 3D-OEM reconstruction is the best reconstruction scheme for quantitative brain FDG-PET studies, and that PSF modelling is unnecessary.

the optimized reconstruction parameters, compared with the routine parameters of each PET centre, improved the quality of PET images, especially the quantitative values of interest for the MEMENTO study.

, in a multicentre trial, the optimization of the reconstruction parameters is recommended to improve the accuracy of the quantitative values, especially in the small structures, at the expense, if any, of a slight degradation of the SNR.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
3D-OSEMs with a high number of iterations and subsets, a large field of view, a high matrix size, a low filter, and a high voxel size are optimal for PET neuroimaging.
the optimized reconstruction is recommended for multicenter trials.
the optimization of the reconstruction parameters of the PET images, using phantom experiments prior the patient studies, is feasible for multicentric PET imaging studies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the absence of PSF modelling reconstruction, the optimized reconstruction parameters should be chosen to improve the smallest sphere RC and ISR.
the optimization of the reconstruction parameters can significantly increase the quality of quantitative measurements, and should be performed for any multicentre study involving PET neuroimaging.
the optimization of 3D-OSEMs reconstruction parameters, without PSF modelling or any other correction, is sufficient for the purpose of quantitative PET neuroimaging in multicentric trials.
